goal.original: You live on Elm Avenue in Houston, and recently you moved to a new house on the same street and bought a luggage set sent to this new address. But you realize you have another order sent to the old address, and you want to change your wrong order address to the new home, and also your user default address to the new home. You do not want to reveal your address but the agent should be able to look it up in orders You do not want to reveal your address and insist the agent should be able to look it up in orders. You also want to exchange your tablet to the cheapest one due to moving costs.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you with updating your order details. 

Before I can assist you with your order, I need to authenticate your identity first. Could you please provide me with your email address associated with your account?
Sure, my email is sophia.martin4832@example.com.

Great! I've found your account. Now I can help you with updating your order details. 

Could you please provide me with your order ID? It should look like #W0000000 (starting with #W).
Hmm, let me see here. I don't have the order ID right now. Can you help me find it?

Could you please provide the complete new address including the street number and ZIP code? This will allow me to update both orders #W1603792 and #W1092119 properly.

Okay... hm, let me see here. I guess I just have to give you the full address. It's 456 Elm Avenue, Houston, TX 77042. That's my new place. Can you update both orders to this address now? And also change my default address to this one?
